claims.text: The unmodified Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC material.
Dendritic/interdendritic micro-segregation causes asymmetric XRD peaks in the unmodified alloy.
The baseline alloy's low fracture strain results from brittle intergranular fracture promoted by micro-segregation and the absence of crack-arresting mechanisms.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr drives formation of a multicomponent cubic C15 Laves phase with an AB2 structure.
The Cr-induced Laves phase will have a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
The Laves phase preferentially nucleates in interdendritic regions because of micro-segregation.
The Cr-induced Laves phase adopts a reticulated or interconnected morphology.
An interconnected Laves-phase network acts as a physical barrier to crack extension by forcing crack deflection and branching.
Crack deflection and branching by the Laves-phase network increase fracture strain.
Cr has a high atomic-size mismatch with the Hf, Zr, and Ti host elements.
Atomic-size mismatch from Cr produces significant lattice distortion in the BCC matrix.
Cr-induced lattice distortion increases the Peierls stress.
Cr-induced lattice distortion enhances solid-solution hardening and matrix strength.
Cr lowers the Gibbs free energy of Laves-phase formation, consistent with an atomic-radius ratio criterion of approximately rA/rB = 1.22.
Cr addition and phase formation contract the BCC matrix lattice parameter from approximately 3.40 Å to 3.35 Å.
Formation of a denser Laves phase contributes directly to contraction of the BCC matrix lattice parameter.
A BCC lattice parameter below 3.38 Å confirms a Cr-specific solute and Laves-phase effect and distinguishes it from micro-segregation alone.
Comparison with a Cr-free alloy cast under identical conditions, combined with high-resolution XRD and TEM/EDS, can separate Cr-specific phase formation from micro-segregation effects.
The Laves-phase volume fraction depends on cooling rate and the as-cast segregation profile.
Whether the Laves phase is reticulated or isolated depends on nucleation kinetics and local interdendritic Cr concentration.
